summary: This is a comment thread from the articulatedrobotics Discourse forum for the 'Running ros2_control on a real robot, making a mobile robot pt 13' tutorial, mainly about the diffdrive_arduino hardware interface. Users report build failures (missing hardware_interface, which needs ros2_control installed on the building machine), a controller manager that fails because of a serial permission error fixed by adding the user to the dialout group, wheel-speed mismatches tied to counts per revolution and loop rate, and incompatibility with ROS Humble because base_interface.hpp was removed. Josh Newans answers most questions, and the thread ends with his clarification that diffdrive_arduino uses a plain serial protocol rather than rosserial or micro-ROS.
one_line: Forum thread troubleshooting the diffdrive_arduino ros2_control hardware interface build, serial permissions, speed tuning and Humble compatibility.
key_facts: Sasffm's diffdrive_arduino build failed with 'Could not find a package configuration file provided by "hardware_interface"', and Josh Newans advised installing ros2_control (e.g. sudo apt install ros-foxy-ros2-control) and installing it on the Pi as well.
Sasffm's controller manager failed with 'IO Exception (13): Permission denied' on the serial device, and the problem was solved by adding the user to the 'dialout' group.
Josh Newans noted that /dev/ttyUSB0 may sometimes be the lidar, so the serial device should be set by path or ID rather than /dev/ttyUSB0.
Josh Newans suggested using 'miniterm -e <device path> 57600' to test the Arduino serial connection.
ketill's robot drove at about half the commanded linear and angular velocity, with counts per revolution of 392 and a wheel radius of 0.09 m and wheel separation of 0.43 m.
Josh Newans calculated that 392 counts per revolution divided by 30 gives 13 counts per loop for 1 rev/sec.
Josh Newans gave an example where 0.5 m/s with a 0.06 m wheel radius needs 1.32 rev/sec, which is about 17 counts per loop.

ketill reported that a Velodyne 16 lidar converted to laser scan could produce too many or too few scans per revolution when the resolution in the YAML file was not evenly divided, and fixed it by setting resolution to 0.006.
Douglas_Beach found that building diffdrive_arduino on ROS Humble failed because hardware_interface/base_interface.hpp no longer exists in the Humble ros2_control package.

BigShark3000 reported that using the HoverDiffDrive plugin on Humble worked after swapping the order of the 'position' and 'velocity' state interfaces in ros2_control.xacro, since the plugin expected position first.
Josh Newans said the Humble incompatibility needs more than a file change, involves a substantial API change, and that he planned a future video on writing a Humble hardware interface.
teknetik reported that a fork at github.com/RedstoneGithub/diffdrive_arduino compiled on Humble but was not yet tested on hardware.
Sudhanshu_ranjan's serial_motor_demo_msgs build failed on ament_cmake not being found, and sourcing /opt/ros/foxy/setup.bash fixed it.
Enno_Stelma used Humble on Ubuntu 22.04 with an RPi4, an Arduino Due running micro-ROS, and an L298N motor driver, and asked whether diffdrive_arduino could work with micro-ROS.

Josh Newans stated that diffdrive_arduino does not use rosserial or micro-ROS, but makes a pure serial connection to software on the other end using a simple custom protocol, so the Arduino should not run rosserial or micro-ROS.
